idiom_name: Django session framework (middleware + pluggable session backends)
implementation_notes: Django supplies the classic manager as SessionMiddleware plus request.session: the store is selected by SESSION_ENGINE (database by default, cached_db, cache, file or the stateless signed_cookies backend) and the identifier is carried in the session cookie. The policy calls exist as methods: django.contrib.auth.login() calls cycle_key() to regenerate the identifier against session fixation, logout() calls flush() to delete the data and the cookie, and set_expiry accepts seconds, a datetime, 0 (expire at browser close) or None. What remains application code is the timeout policy and cookie hardening (SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY is on by default; Secure and SameSite are settings).
pitfalls: Reading a session is not activity for expiry purposes: Django computes expiry from the last modification, so a fetch-only workload can expire a session that is used constantly.
The cache backend loses sessions when entries are evicted or the cache restarts; the documentation recommends cached_db for production.
The signed_cookies backend is signed but not encrypted and is not invalidated by logout, so a stolen cookie stays usable until SESSION_COOKIE_AGE; it cannot satisfy central invalidation.
Non-JSON-serializable values or non-string keys silently change data between requests under the default JSON serializer.
